title: Temporal Compute
question: What computation is still useful when its value depends on when it finishes?
summary: A deterministic Rust simulator for jobs whose value depends on completion time, and a Python harness that drives a real renderer. Generation I asked which waiting job should run next and lost to EDF; it is retired. Generation II asks, given the intermediate state, which unit of computation is worth doing next — allocating render samples by marginal value.
architecture: tc-core → tc-ir (TOML scenarios) → tc-scheduler (FIFO, fixed priority, EDF, temporal utility, utility density)
tc-sim — deterministic, single-CPU, non-preemptive discrete events; JSONL traces and metrics; tc-cli
Generation II — a Python harness driving PBRT-v4 on the CPU, pinned to one commit, with contracts and evidence under research/
maturity: Generation I complete and negative; Generation II's primary experiment is preregistered and not run

experiments.title: Seven toy fixtures
experiments.hypothesis: Explicit completion-time utility improves mission utility over deadline-only scheduling.
experiments.setup: 7 fixtures × 5 policies, run twice with byte-for-byte trace replay.
experiments.result: Utility density wins the mixed fixture (4,370 against EDF 353); EDF wins deadline pressure (160 against 100); density loses its own trap fixture by 100 points.
experiments.limitations: Semantic evidence only — it refutes 'the greedy policies always beat EDF', and proves nothing at scale.

experiments.title: Temporal utility against EDF, at scale
experiments.hypothesis: The temporal-utility scheduler earns at least 5% more utility than the strongest conventional baseline.
experiments.setup: Protocol frozen before the run. 200 synthetic Earth-observation scenarios × 48 tasks (9,600 jobs), 15,882 runs; five registered gates.
experiments.baseline: FIFO, fixed priority, EDF, EDF + priority
experiments.result: 524,509 against EDF's 552,525 — 5.07% worse. Wins/ties/losses 15/15/170. All 12 sensitivity variants negative. Failed all five gates. The utility-density variant came within 0.35% of EDF.
experiments.limitations: No simulation parameter is a measured mission quantity. Temporal utility let 1,203 cloud jobs expire unstarted, against EDF's 37.

experiments.title: Renderer qualification
experiments.hypothesis: A production renderer can meet five accounting and estimator requirements.
experiments.setup: Mitsuba 3.9.1 and PBRT-v4 evaluated against the contract.
experiments.limitations: Infrastructure gate, not a scientific result.

experiments.title: PBRT accounting contract
experiments.hypothesis: PBRT's sample accounting can be proven complete on native fixtures.
experiments.result: Fixtures pass; the complete-envelope proof is not established. Fails to qualify.

experiments.title: Transmission and triangle coverage
experiments.hypothesis: The extended fixtures close the accounting gap.
experiments.setup: Native fixtures in CI; 1,952 transmission events.
experiments.measurement: Camera, continuation and charged ray counts per fixture
experiments.result: Pass. PBRT-v4 on the CPU is selected as the kernel.

experiments.title: Bridge, streams and failure containment
experiments.hypothesis: The bridge, paired streams, ray accounting and failure containment hold on a bounded matrix.
experiments.result: Pass on the bounded matrix; the per-sample maximum is 13.
experiments.limitations: Says nothing about baseline competence, policy quality or time benefit at primary scale.

experiments.title: Are the baselines competent?
experiments.hypothesis: The comparators are competent and the controller is distinguishable from them.
experiments.setup: Synthetic fields without the renderer, 3 seeds.
experiments.result: Neither conventional baseline is competent (MC-UCB drifts 0.36–0.67 against a 0.05 limit). The controller differs from variance-guided only through its recent-improvement term.
experiments.limitations: Led to an amendment of the baselines before any primary run.

experiments.title: Amended baselines
experiments.result: Go: drift 0. But the cost lever is 0.098, under the 0.10 threshold — the controller is distinct only through a noisy term.
experiments.limitations: An open question remains whether a controller that differs mainly through noise is a meaningful test of the hypothesis.

experiments.title: Marginal-value sample allocation (primary)
experiments.hypothesis: A state-aware marginal-value controller allocates rendering work more efficiently than uniform sampling and a strong adaptive baseline.
experiments.setup: Preregistered: 10 scenes × 8 seeds. Pass requires ≥ 10% relative-MSE reduction and ≥ 5% time benefit.
experiments.measurement: Relative MSE at equal cost; wall time
experiments.result: Not run. The next-step review found the controller collapses to variance-guided under equal cost, and projects 1,800–4,200 single-worker hours per pass.
experiments.limitations: No outcomes, references or freeze tag exist yet.
